html:
A book of scripture published in 1830 in Palmyra, New York, by Joseph Smith. It became the founding text of the Latter Day Saint movement.

Smith said an angel named Moroni had led him to golden plates buried in a hill, and that he translated them by divine power. The book tells of Israelites who sailed to the Americas around 600 BCE and split into two peoples, the Nephites and the Lamanites. Its high point is a visit by the risen Jesus to the Americas. Historians and archaeologists find no evidence for these peoples.

It appeared in upstate New York at the height of the Second Great Awakening, when new churches were springing up. Smith founded his church in April 1830. His followers faced hostility as they moved to Ohio, Missouri and Illinois, where Smith was killed by a mob in 1844.

Brigham Young then led most of them west to Utah in 1847, along a trail near the Oregon Trail. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints now has millions of members worldwide.
sum: A book of scripture published in 1830 in Palmyra, New York, by Joseph Smith. It became the founding text of the Latter Day Saint movement.
